status_summary: An executive order of 2025-01-23 bars executive agencies from taking action to establish, issue or promote a central bank digital currency in the United States or abroad and directs that any ongoing plans be terminated. A statutory bar followed in mid-2026: the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644, Public Law 119-101, Sec. 1101), which includes a provision barring the Federal Reserve Board and Reserve Banks from issuing or creating a CBDC (or something substantially similar), directly or through intermediaries, passed the Senate 85 to 5 and the House 358 to 32 in June 2026 and became law without the President's signature, with the public law dated 2026-07-11 (one trade report places it a day earlier). The prohibition expires on 2030-12-31, and a Duke blog notes that the statute's digital asset definition may leave a CBDC on a centralized ledger outside its text. The separate House-passed Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act (H.R. 1919, 2025-07-17) would impose a broader ban; the Senate companion (S. 1124) was reported to be in committee as of March 2026 (secondary source). The Fed's own CBDC page still shows only its 2022 discussion paper and describes no program. Separately, Congress enacted the GENIUS Act on stablecoins in July 2025, and the Fed issued proposals in September 2026 for a GENIUS Act stablecoin issuer framework.

timeline.event: Executive order on digital financial technology prohibits agencies from establishing, issuing or promoting a CBDC and directs termination of any ongoing CBDC plans (Section 5); it also sets up a working group on digital asset markets.
House passed H.R. 1919, the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, prohibiting Federal Reserve Banks from issuing a CBDC and the Board from testing, studying or developing one (engrossed House text).
GENIUS Act signed (Public Law 119-27), creating a federal framework for payment stablecoins; it does not itself create or bar a CBDC per the summary read.

Congress passes the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which contains a time-limited prohibition on the Federal Reserve issuing a CBDC (Senate 85 to 5, House 358 to 32; month only, first of month used, because sources differ on the exact dates and order).

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) becomes Public Law 119-101, dated 2026-07-11 in the law's header. Its table of contents lists Sec. 1101, 'Central bank digital currency,' which the House Financial Services Committee's section-by-section describes as barring the Federal Reserve from issuing a CBDC until the end of 2030 (expiring 2030-12-31). The Duke FinReg Blog reports that it became law without the President's signature and that it covers the Board and Reserve Banks, directly or through intermediaries; The Block places the event on the prior Friday (2026-07-10). The operative text of Sec. 1101 could not be read in the fetched portion.
Federal Reserve announced proposals for a GENIUS Act stablecoin issuer framework, open for comment.

uncertainties: Pass 5: the public law number (119-101), its 2026-07-11 date and the section (Sec. 1101) are confirmed from the GovInfo page for the enrolled law and its table of contents, and the 2030-12-31 sunset from the House Financial Services Committee's section-by-section; the operative text of Sec. 1101 was not reachable by the research tool (the fetch was truncated before Title XI, and congress.gov blocks fetchers), so the scope (directly or through intermediaries), the digital asset definition and the exemptions still rest on the Duke blog and law-firm analyses, and the no-signature detail on press reports. Sources conflict on the order of House and Senate passage. The GENIUS Act date and number come from a Wikipedia summary. Whether the Fed has formally ended CBDC research was not verified beyond the age of its CBDC page. The chapter's other monetary options (free banking, commodity-backed money, a commission on alternatives to the Fed, limits on lender of last resort) were not researched and no action on them was seen.
